name: Gauss’s least-squares orbital estimation
description: Gauss developed an account of least-squares estimation for astronomical observations.

impact.note: Gave astronomers and surveyors a probabilistic reason and working procedure for combining discordant observations; the theory of errors and geodetic adjustment grew from his account.

date.basis: Year of the cited publication or dated report; not necessarily the date work began.

events.statement: Gauss published an account of least squares in his 1809 treatise on celestial orbits.

evidence.supports: Describes Gauss’s 1809 exposition in orbital determination and notes Legendre’s prior publication.

contributions.resource: Contributed to the documented Gauss’s least-squares orbital estimation work.

evidence.supports: Describes Gauss’s 1809 exposition in orbital determination and notes Legendre’s prior publication.

earliest_record.rationale: A dated witness within the evidence collected here; not a claim of global priority or earliest observation.

caveats: Legendre published the method before Gauss; priority of earlier independent use was disputed. The dated episode is Gauss’s publication, not the method’s invention.

research.note: Independent source reading checked the dated events and associated claims. Grain and other facets remain provisional.

links.statement: Gauss’s orbit calculations used the Keplerian conic model, whose elliptical form Kepler had earlier applied to Mars.

evidence.locator: Discussion of Theoria Motus and planetary observations
evidence.supports: Describes Gauss’s computing the motion of a body in a conic section according to Kepler’s laws.
